source.title: Snoopy: An Online Interface for Exploring the Effect of Pretraining Term Frequencies on Few-Shot LM Performance
source.authors: Yasaman Razeghi; Raja Sekhar Reddy Mekala; IV RobertL.Logan; Matt Gardner; Sameer Singh

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The paper presents an interface for relating pretraining term frequencies to few-shot benchmark accuracy. It does not test scaling-law loss, extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation, or the other listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports qualitative accuracy-versus-term-frequency findings, not results about loss scaling or performance prediction from model scale or pretraining loss. Those adjacent findings are recorded with versions ["none"]. Other interface plots and demonstrations have no stated outcome beyond showing the plots.
record.test_reason: A demo paper presenting an interface that relates Pile term frequencies to few-shot accuracy. It cites Kaplan et al. only to say scale drives improvement. The interface lets users choose among GPT-Neo-1.3B, GPT-Neo-2.7B and GPT-J-6B, but the paper reports no result across model sizes, no loss and no scaling fit. Its stated findings are qualitative frequency/term-presence comparisons for GPT-J-6B only, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: the authors present Snoopy as a tool for studying how pretraining term frequencies affect few-shot performance without expensive compute, and hope it eases such research.
record.recipe_differences: The study provides term-frequency statistics and precomputed few-shot accuracy visualizations; it does not fit or evaluate scaling laws for held-out loss.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported term-presence comparison differs by dataset: the “he” advantage is stated for SST but not for WNLI or TriviaQA.

fits_no_version.finding: GPT-J-6B few-shot accuracy correlates strongly with pretraining term frequency on multiplication (qualitative). On SST, instances with 'he' score much higher than those with 'she'; this does not hold on WNLI or TriviaQA.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Few-shot accuracy is associated with pretraining term frequency and term presence, varying by task.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, System Demonstrations (2022)
record.problems: The reported case-study findings are qualitative and do not provide exact accuracy values, statistical uncertainty, or a quantified correlation. The paper does not run scaling, loss, or compute-allocation experiments.
record.rows_left_out: Figures 3, 5, and 9 and other interface examples are not recorded because the text does not state an outcome for them beyond displaying plots.

untested.parts: No loss measurements or scaling fits.
No other modality or training regime is studied.
Model-size options exist in the interface (1.3B–6B), but no across-size downstream result is reported.

record.verdict_notes: Relation changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only': Kaplan et al. appears only as a motivating citation. All rows correctly carry versions ['none'].

versions.untested_parts: No scale- or pretraining-loss-based prediction of downstream performance is tested.
